children: Bitcoin dropped to an intraday low of $57,716 on November 20, 2026, its lowest price since September 2024. The slide of more than 6% erased every gain the asset had made since Donald Trump's re-election.
The drop also leaves Bitcoin down more than 50% from its all-time high above $126,000, set in October 2025.
The selling did not happen in a vacuum. Approximately $2 billion in long positions were liquidated across the crypto market in the 24 hours leading up to the November 20 drop.
As Bitcoin slipped below $60,000, $94.6 million in long positions were wiped out in a single hour across Binance, Bybit and OKX.

Meanwhile, US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have seen sustained outflows. On November 19 alone, those funds recorded net outflows of $582 million. When investors pull money from these funds, the selling pressure tends to land on the underlying asset.
The decline came alongside a wider sell-off across global markets, with risk assets such as technology stocks taking a notable hit.

The VIX index also climbed as Bitcoin fell. The VIX is often called Wall Street's fear gauge, since it tracks expected volatility in US stocks, and a rising reading signals that investors are bracing for bumpier conditions.
Traders have shifted into a risk-off posture, with a stronger dollar and uncertainty over the direction of monetary policy adding to that defensive mood.

Bitcoin rallied after Trump's re-election, and that momentum eventually carried it to a record above $126,000 in October 2025. The intraday low of $57,716 now sits below the levels that preceded that entire run.

The arrival of spot Bitcoin ETFs had been widely seen as a source of steady institutional demand. The $582 million in single-day outflows on November 19 shows that same plumbing can work just as efficiently in reverse.

For traders, the clearest lesson is about leverage. Roughly $2 billion in liquidated longs over 24 hours shows how much borrowed money was riding on higher prices, and how quickly that bet turned into forced selling.
For longer-term holders, the more important signal may be the ETF flows. Sustained outflows suggest that some investors who entered through regulated funds are reducing exposure.
With Bitcoin moving in step with tech stocks and the VIX, factors such as the strength of the dollar and shifts in monetary policy appear to be steering crypto prices more than crypto-specific news.

title: Bitcoin falls to its lowest level since September 2024
